clue.text: Noble Roman's head's buried by a fragrant shrub

indicators.note: the leading letter of the name is pushed down below the surface, further into the word

parts.note: Brutus is Shakespeare's 'noblest Roman of them all' in Julius Caesar

explanation.surface: A Roman aristocrat's head is buried beneath a sweet-smelling bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head's buried' sinks the leading letter one place down into the name; 'by' simply sets the article alongside.
explanation.definitionFit: The strawberry tree, genus Arbutus, is an evergreen shrub with scented flowers.

clue.text: Vessels guarding current Roman HQ

indicators.note: the two containers stand on either side of the current, protecting it between them

parts.note: a vat is a large vessel for liquids
a can is a metal vessel or container
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Ships protect a modern Roman headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' does double duty in the surface as ships, but here supplies two different containers, with 'guarding' setting the current between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican is the seat of the papacy in Rome, the headquarters of the Roman Catholic Church.

clue.text: Media operatives turned up and worked without me

parts.note: to turn up is to arrive, to come; past tense came

indicators.note: used in the old sense of outside, so the word for worked wraps round the clue's me

parts.note: a machine that ran was working

explanation.surface: Journalists arrived and laboured without my help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'turned up' means arrived, not reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Camera operators work in film and television, so they are media workers.

clue.text: Retiring setter, sixty, consuming unknown stuff in plane perhaps

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, going back, so the whole run is read from right to left

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

indicators.note: the Roman numeral eats the unknown, taking it inside

parts.note: LX is sixty in Roman numerals
Y is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A shy crossword compiler of sixty eats something mysterious on an aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' turns ME + LYX into XYLEM; 'plane' is the plane tree, not an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Xylem is the woody water-carrying tissue found in plants such as the plane tree.

clue.text: Wooden counter without opening surrounds area

indicators.note: what is left of the counter goes round the abbreviation for area
the first letter of the word for counter is dropped

parts.note: a token is a counter used in games

explanation.surface: A wooden shop counter with no gap encloses a space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without opening' takes T off TOKEN to leave OKEN, and 'surrounds' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oaken means made of oak timber, so it is a literary word for wooden.

clue.text: Most anxious jazz great heading off in pursuit

indicators.note: the shortened name is placed inside the word for pursuit

parts.note: a quest is a search or pursuit

indicators.note: the leading letter of the musician's name is removed

parts.note: Count Basie was a great jazz bandleader and pianist

explanation.surface: A jazz legend sets off in a nervous chase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jazz great' is Count Basie, the bandleader; 'heading off' beheads him, and 'in' places the remainder inside the word for pursuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Queasy can mean uneasy or nervous, so the superlative is most uneasy.

clue.text: What's to prevent shocking abuse primarily in offensive recording?

indicators.note: the single letter goes inside the word for offensive

parts.note: insulting means offensive

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word abuse is wanted

parts.note: a tape is a recording

explanation.surface: How to stop scandalous abuse showing up in a rude recording?
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' gives A, which 'in' places in INSULTING; 'shocking' means electric shocks, not scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical tape covers bare wires to stop someone getting an electric shock.

clue.text: Restricted sources of intelligence — for the military?

definitions.meaning: fee-paying schools: private means restricted to some, and schools are where intelligence is formed
read playfully as schools for privates, the lowest-ranking soldiers

explanation.walkthrough: PRIVATE is 'restricted' and SCHOOLS are 'sources of intelligence'; the second reading jokes that these places teach army privates. In Britain, private schools are fee-paying independent schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Independent fee-paying schools are restricted to those who can pay, and schools educate minds.

clue.text: Something to stimulate record turnover in exotic parties?

indicators.note: the reversed record sits inside the rearranged letters
exotic means strange or foreign, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the record is turned over, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Something to excite a record sale at foreign parties?
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges the parties, 'turnover' turns the record round, and 'in' puts the turned record inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter dish or drink is served to stimulate the appetite before a meal.

clue.text: A bit of grit stuck into bare elbow

indicators.note: the letter is pushed inside the word for bare

parts.note: nude means bare, unclothed

indicators.note: a bit here is just the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A speck of grit lodged in an uncovered elbow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of' gives G, which 'stuck into' puts inside NUDE. 'elbow' is a verb here, not the joint.
explanation.definitionFit: To elbow someone is to push or prod them with the arm, which is to nudge them.

clue.text: Famous revolutionary captured in Kingston on vacation

indicators.note: the turned-round word goes inside the town's remaining letters
the town is vacated, emptied of its inner letters, leaving its ends
the following word is turned round, as in a revolution

parts.note: won means captured, taken in battle

explanation.surface: A well-known rebel was arrested in Kingston while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' is not a rebel but an instruction to turn the word for captured round; 'on vacation' empties the town's middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something known is widely recognised, which is what famous means.

clue.text: Obsessive thief sits in resort

indicators.note: re-sorted, the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A compulsive burglar is sitting in a holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday town, but split as re-sort it tells you to rearrange the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetishist has an obsessive fixation on some object or practice.

clue.text: Mawkish Liberal's supplanted her in perfidy

indicators.note: one thing takes the place of another, here the abbreviation for Liberal ousting the clue's her

parts.note: treachery means perfidy, betrayal
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A sentimental Liberal has replaced a woman in an act of betrayal.
explanation.walkthrough: In TREACHERY, 'supplanted' replaces HER with L, the Liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacly means sickly sweet, like treacle, so overly sentimental.

clue.text: Felicity departs with crew crossing loch

parts.note: D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

indicators.note: the crew stretches across the loch, enclosing it

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew
L is a map abbreviation for loch, a Scottish lake

explanation.surface: Felicity sets off with her rowing team across a Scottish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts L in EIGHT. 'Felicity' looks like a woman's name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Felicity is great happiness, and delight is great pleasure.

clue.text: Radio presenter needing a new job shortly

indicators.note: the word for job is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a chore is a small job

explanation.surface: A broadcaster needs another job soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims CHORE to CHOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor is the main presenter who holds a broadcast programme together.

clue.text: Clown making impact with support of family

indicators.note: in a down answer, the supporting piece goes beneath, so family comes after

parts.note: a bump is a collision or impact
kin means family

explanation.surface: A circus clown makes an impression with his family behind him.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumpkin is an unsophisticated rustic, a clumsy oaf or clown.

clue.text: Hairy specimen is snatched from a naturalist abroad

indicators.note: the letters of the clue's is are taken away from the pool
abroad means scattered, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hairy creature is grabbed from a field biologist overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I and S out of A NATURALIST and 'abroad' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a large hairy spider, so a hairy example of wildlife.

clue.text: Result of suburban aftershock for characters in bar?

parts.note: a semi, a semi-detached house, is the typical suburban home
after a shock, a house might quiver, so it quavers

explanation.surface: What happens after an earthquake in the suburbs, to some marks in a bar?
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'a semi quavers' after the shock. A semi is a British semi-detached house; 'bar' is a bar of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Semiquavers are sixteenth notes, symbols written within a bar of music.

clue.text: Lead from elevated part of church ultimately nicked

indicators.note: in a down answer, raising a word turns it to read upwards
the final letter is stolen

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church

explanation.surface: Lead roofing stolen from a raised section of a church at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately nicked' cuts NAVE to NAV, and 'elevated' turns it upward. 'nicked' is British slang for stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: The van, short for vanguard, is the leading part of an army or movement.

clue.text: Where ranchers may flourish by cutting meals

indicators.note: the multiplication sign cuts into the word for meals

parts.note: tea is a meal in British usage
X is the times sign, as in two by four

explanation.surface: Cattle farmers could thrive by cutting back on food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' puts X ('by', as in 3 by 4) inside TEAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Texas is the US state famous for cattle ranching.

clue.text: Tree topped with carbon a possible result of eruption

indicators.note: in a down answer the tree has the carbon on top of it

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
the alder is a tree

explanation.surface: A tree crowned with soot might come from a volcanic blast.
explanation.definitionFit: A caldera is a large crater formed when a volcano collapses after an eruption.

clue.text: Feature of vacuum that's unimportant

definitions.meaning: a vacuum is a space empty of all substance
a phrase saying it doesn't matter

explanation.definitionFit: A vacuum contains no substance at all, and a thing of no consequence is irrelevant.

clue.text: Consider cutting devices badly drawn

indicators.note: the word for consider cuts into the word devices
the combined letters are put together badly, in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
to rate something is to consider or judge it

explanation.surface: Look at cutting tools that have been poorly designed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' and 'badly' both act: the word for consider is set into devices and then the letters are scrambled. 'drawn' is the butcher's sense, not the artist's.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a carcass is to take out its innards; eviscerated means disembowelled.

clue.text: Weed in estate well clear of borders

parts.note: the grounds are an estate's land

indicators.note: the word well loses its outside letters

explanation.surface: A weed growing on an estate, well away from the flowerbeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear of borders' strips W and L from 'well', leaving EL; 'borders' looks like flowerbeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundsel is a common garden weed of the daisy family.

clue.text: Quality university favourite to include grading

indicators.note: the word for favourite takes in the word for grading

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
a mark is a grade awarded

explanation.surface: A good university's top student is included in assessments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quality' is an adjective here, as in quality goods, matching the answer's sense of high-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Upmarket goods are of superior quality and aimed at wealthier buyers.

clue.text: Cave in simple, unlimited verse

indicators.note: without limits, the word simple loses its first and last letters

parts.note: an ode is a poem, a piece of verse

explanation.surface: In a cave, simple poetry goes on without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unlimited' cuts SIMPLE to IMPL. 'Cave in' looks like a hollow, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To implode is to collapse inwards, which is what caving in means.

clue.text: Clipped language describing barking dog in digs

indicators.note: describing in the sense of drawing a line round, so the shortened word encloses the rest
the word is clipped, losing its last letter

parts.note: lingo is informal for a language

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A curt tongue talks of a yapping hound in its quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clipped', 'barking' and 'describing' all act: describing in the geometric sense of drawing round. 'barking' is British slang for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs is British informal for rented rooms, a place of lodging.

clue.text: Bearing east, large and small fliers get lost

indicators.note: the airline carries the compass point within it

parts.note: the large fliers are British Airways, BA
a tit is a small bird

explanation.surface: Heading east, big and little birds lose their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large and small fliers' are an airline and a bird, not two birds; 'Bearing' means carrying, so the airline holds the compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat it is a slang command to go away, just like get lost.

clue.text: Jacket or cape one oddball's taken up

indicators.note: in a down answer, raised means the letters read upwards

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
I is the Roman numeral for one
a nut is an eccentric, an oddball

explanation.surface: A jacket or cloak worn by an eccentric is shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken up' turns C + I + NUT around.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a close-fitting jacket, especially as part of a uniform.

clue.text: Small fish queen's taken from boat

indicators.note: the queen's letters are removed from the boat

parts.note: a ferry is a boat
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A tiddler belonging to the Queen is removed from a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is taken out of FERRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Fry are young fish just hatched.
